body.text: Now rewrite the R4/R5 tests to match the corrected semantics — including a regression test encoding the exact live misfire:
Now update the ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3 flowchart to match the corrected semantics:

attributes.command: cd C:/src/git-for-ai/packages/core && pnpm build 2>&1 | tail -4 && pnpm vitest run src/identity 2>&1 | tail -8
cd C:/src/git-for-ai/packages/core && pnpm vitest run src/git src/ledger src/sessions 2>&1 | tail -4 && cd ../cli && pnpm vitest run 2>&1 | tail -4

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git add packages/core/src/identity/resolve.ts packages/core/src/identity/identity.test.ts architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix R4: infer missed rewrites from sibling diff overlap, not tree similarity

D1 from PLAN_2026-07-18.md §1.2, proven by live dogfood data (8e25afb
and 7d4cd73 — unrelated commits — glued into one change). The old
signal was wrong on both axes: whole-tree similarity is ~1 for any
small commit in a non-tiny repo, and a CHILD commit is virtually never
the same logical change as its parent — rewrites (amend/reword/rebase)
produce SIBLINGS, not children.

R4 now models the actual missed-rewrite shape: the commit has one
parent P, some change's head is also a sole child of P, and the two
commits' changed-path sets (each diffed against P) overlap >= 0.6
Jaccard (was: 0.7 whole-tree). Best-overlap candidate wins; folded
entries are skipped; heads missing from the repo just don't match.

Tests: rewritten R4 suite — hooks-missed amend infers correctly; a
below-threshold sibling mints fresh; and a regression test encoding
the exact D1 misfire (trailerless child of a known commit) now
asserting R5. ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3 flowchart updated to match.

The two miswired dogfood entries are repaired separately via relink
(next W1 item).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
